# SDT-004 tier 1 — the hand-curated membership list.
#
# Tier 1 is "high-confidence, prefix-anchored provider rules": rules whose
# matched credential carries a literal, provider-specific prefix, so a match is
# structurally the credential rather than a guess about one. Membership is
# editorial (that is what a confidence tier is); the refresh script enforces the
# mechanical half — the id must exist upstream at the pinned digest, the regex
# must be taken verbatim, and a rule with more than one capture group is
# rejected rather than guessed at.
#
# Generic and entropy-adjacent rules (`generic-api-key` and friends) are NOT
# tier 1. They are where false-positive volume lives, and CIB-373 is already
# open on that class. They are a later tier with its own measurement.
#
# One id per line. `#` comments and blank lines are ignored.

# --- GitLab -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Every GitLab credential class carries its own `gl*-` prefix.
# `gitlab-pat-routable` and `gitlab-runner-authentication-token-routable` are
# deliberately EXCLUDED: a routable token also matches its non-routable sibling
# (`glpat-`/`glrt-`), and both would be high-confidence, so one credential would
# report twice. The sibling already covers the prefix.
gitlab-cicd-job-token
gitlab-deploy-token
gitlab-feature-flag-client-token
gitlab-feed-token
gitlab-incoming-mail-token
gitlab-kubernetes-agent-token
gitlab-oauth-app-secret
gitlab-pat
gitlab-ptt
gitlab-rrt
gitlab-runner-authentication-token
gitlab-scim-token
gitlab-session-cookie

# --- DigitalOcean -----------------------------------------------------------
digitalocean-access-token
digitalocean-pat
digitalocean-refresh-token

# --- Shopify ----------------------------------------------------------------
shopify-access-token
shopify-custom-access-token
shopify-private-app-access-token
shopify-shared-secret

# --- Postman ----------------------------------------------------------------
postman-api-token

# --- Mailgun ---------------------------------------------------------------
# `mailgun-signing-key` is EXCLUDED: its secret is a bare
# `[a-h0-9]{32}-[a-h0-9]{8}-[a-h0-9]{8}` run with no literal provider prefix,
# so it fails the tier-1 criterion.
mailgun-private-api-token
mailgun-pub-key

# --- New Relic --------------------------------------------------------------
# `new-relic-user-api-id` is EXCLUDED: its secret is a bare `[a-z0-9]{64}` run
# with no literal prefix — entropy-adjacent, not prefix-anchored.
new-relic-browser-api-token
new-relic-insert-key
new-relic-user-api-key

# --- Slack ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only the webhook URL. Slack's `xox[baprs]-` bot/user tokens are already
# covered by the built-in `Slack Token` rule; vendoring gitleaks' siblings would
# double-report one credential.
slack-webhook-url

# --- Deliberate exclusions, recorded so they are not re-litigated silently ---
# sendgrid-api-token   duplicate of the built-in `SendGrid API Key` shape
#                      (`SG.` + 22 + `.` + 43 = the same 66 characters).
# private-key          upstream regex is block-scoped
#                      (`-----BEGIN…-----[\s\S-]{64,}?KEY-----`) and Anvil's
#                      scanner is line-local, so it cannot be vendored verbatim.
#                      Anvil already carries line-local `Private Key` and
#                      `PGP Private Key` built-ins; widening those to cover
#                      `OPENSSH`/`EC` headers is a built-in change, not a
#                      vendoring one.
# generic-api-key      tier 2 by construction (see the header note).
